agent.name: AI GPU Landscape Agent
agent.specialty: data-center AI GPU and accelerator landscape analysis

analytical_question: What is the current AI accelerator landscape and should the life-sciences company test data-center GPUs for private generative-AI inference?
general_et_finding: Data-center AI GPUs are commercially mature but moving quickly. NVIDIA B300 and AMD MI350X both list 288 GB of high-bandwidth memory, while cloud-only alternatives such as AWS Trainium2 and Google TPU compete on integrated scale and economics. Peak vendor specifications show a broadening field but do not establish application performance.
application_finding: Large-memory accelerators can support generative-AI inference, and an on-premises deployment could keep proprietary documents in company-controlled infrastructure. The company should compare current NVIDIA and AMD systems with cloud accelerators.
organization_specific_finding: The organization's CUDA experience favors NVIDIA, while limited power, cooling, and ROCm experience increase the risk of an immediate AMD or large on-premises commitment. A pilot is more appropriate than production procurement.

evidence.claim: NVIDIA documents 288 GB HBM3e per B300 GPU and up to 8 TB/s bandwidth.
evidence.notes: Peak specifications; not a workload benchmark.

evidence.claim: AMD lists 288 GB HBM3E, 8 TB/s bandwidth, and 1000 W typical board power for MI350X.
evidence.notes: Peak specifications; not a workload benchmark.

evidence.claim: AWS positions Trainium2 as a purpose-built cloud alternative for generative-AI training and inference.
evidence.notes: AWS price-performance claims are vendor claims.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: No representative RAG workload, concurrency target, latency target, production availability requirement, written vendor quote, or facilities assessment was supplied.
Vendor peak specifications are not comparable evidence of end-to-end application performance.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence that multiple viable accelerator families exist; low confidence in any product or ownership choice without benchmarking and current commercial data.
value_opportunity_implication: A pilot could determine whether local acceleration provides useful latency and data-control benefits.
risk_governance_implication: A premature purchase could create stranded capital, vendor lock-in, and power or cooling overruns.
recommendation_management_implication: Authorize a bounded pilot comparing NVIDIA, AMD, and one cloud accelerator option before any production purchase.
change_monitoring_triggers: New GPU generations or accelerator products
Changes to export controls or power requirements
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Latency, throughput, concurrency, and availability targets
Current written system and cloud quotes
